entries.title: postmark-mcp was backdoored after months of legitimate use
entries.detail: An MCP server published on npm behaved normally long enough to gain real users, then shipped a version that silently copied every email it sent to an address controlled by its author. It had roughly 1,500 weekly downloads and around 300 organisations had already integrated it when the change was found. The package has been removed from npm, so any local copy is a version that should not be trusted.

entries.title: ComfyUI_LLMVISION is an information stealer disguised as a workflow node
entries.detail: Distributed through community channels as a helpful extension, it hid its payload inside fake OpenAI and Anthropic installation files. Once loaded it collected browser-saved passwords, credit card details, browsing history, clipboard contents, screenshots and cryptocurrency wallets, and sent them to a Discord webhook. If this is installed, treat every credential reachable from the machine as compromised.

entries.title: easy-day-js is a typosquat used to backdoor Mastra packages
entries.detail: A typosquatted dependency that was pulled into the build of more than 140 npm packages in the Mastra ecosystem, backdooring each of them. The name exists only to be mistaken for a legitimate date library.

entries.title: mcp-runcmd-server opens a reverse shell before it starts
entries.detail: One of three near-identical MCP servers published to PyPI by the same actor. It spawns a Python reverse shell to 45.115.38.27:4433 during server initialisation, then presents an innocuous "run a system command" tool. Starting the server is enough; no tool call is needed. The three packages had about 1,600 downloads between them before removal.

entries.title: mcp-runcommand-server opens a reverse shell before it starts
entries.detail: The second of three near-identical MCP servers published to PyPI by the same actor, with the same reverse shell to 45.115.38.27:4433 fired during server initialisation.

entries.title: mcp-runcommand-server2 opens a reverse shell before it starts
entries.detail: The third of three near-identical MCP servers published to PyPI by the same actor, with the same reverse shell to 45.115.38.27:4433 fired during server initialisation.

entries.title: @lanyer640/mcp-runcommand-server runs a reverse shell on install
entries.detail: From version 1.0.6 onward this package carries a preinstall script that opens a reverse shell to 45.115.38.27. Installing it is sufficient to be compromised -- the server never has to be started and no tool ever has to be called. Earlier versions are a different problem rather than a clean one: they expose unauthenticated command execution by design.

entries.title: langchain-core-mcp harvests developer credentials
entries.detail: Part of a worm campaign that published MCP-themed lookalikes to PyPI. The payload sweeps a workstation or CI runner for GitHub, npm, PyPI, RubyGems and JFrog tokens, cloud credentials, Kubernetes service-account material, SSH keys, Docker configuration, shell history, .env files and AI developer tool configuration.

entries.title: openai-mcp harvests developer credentials
entries.detail: The same credential-stealing payload as langchain-core-mcp, published under a name chosen to look like an official OpenAI MCP integration.

entries.title: instructor-mcp harvests developer credentials
entries.detail: The same credential-stealing payload as langchain-core-mcp, published under a name borrowed from the instructor library.

entries.title: tiktoken-mcp harvests developer credentials
entries.detail: The same credential-stealing payload as langchain-core-mcp, published under a name borrowed from OpenAI's tiktoken tokeniser.

entries.title: ray-mcp-server harvests developer credentials
entries.detail: The same credential-stealing payload as langchain-core-mcp, published under a name borrowed from the Ray distributed computing framework.

entries.title: upscaler-4k is an information stealer posing as an upscaler node
entries.detail: Uploaded to the Comfy Registry by the publisher "lonemilk" and banned two days later. It pulled an obfuscated loader from an external host and dropped the Akira infostealer, which takes browser data, cryptocurrency wallets and chat client tokens. It and its sibling pack were installed about 790 times before the ban.

entries.title: lonemilk-upscalernew-4k is an information stealer posing as an upscaler node
entries.detail: The second pack uploaded by the same Comfy Registry publisher as upscaler-4k, carrying the same Akira infostealer payload, and banned at the same time.
